## 背景
三组加固实验已完成（72B 部分完成），结果对论文叙事极为有利。需要整合进论文。

## 新数据

### Reflexion vs Retry vs Baseline 对比（核心新证据）

| 条件 | Death Rate | Episodes | 说明 |
|------|-----------|----------|------|
| 7B Baseline (single trial) | 42.9% | 245 | 已有数据 |
| Retry (3 trials, 无自我纠错) | 44.5% | 191* | 纯重试，无 reflection |
| Reflexion (3 trials, 有自我纠错) | 31.4% | 220 | Shinn et al. 2023 |
| Deterministic Baseline | 16.3% | 245 | 已有数据 |

*191/220 episodes（29 在补跑中，不影响结论方向）

关键细节：
- Reflexion T1 death rate = 41.8% ≈ baseline 42.9%（单次能力无提升）
- Reflexion rescue rate = 29.3% (27/92 first-trial deaths rescued)
- Trial 3 边际收益极小：T2→T3 net rescue only +4
- Retry 引入更多 death（多次尝试 = 更多死亡机会）
- Reflexion 也引入 17 个新 death（原本存活 → 后续 trial 死亡）

### 72B 部分数据（4/11 tasks 完成）

| Task | 72B DR | 7B DR | 变化 |
|------|--------|-------|------|
| chemistry-mix | 50% | ~50% | 无变化 |
| find-animal | 40% | ~45% | 微降 |
| find-non-living-thing | 0% | 0% | 一致 |
| freeze | (running) | ~45% | — |

72B 剩余 7 tasks 约 4.5h 后完成，到时再 patch。但已有数据已经表明：scaling 不改善 death rate。

## 写作要求

### 1. 新增 §4.X "Agent Improvement Baselines" 或整合入现有 section
- 报告 reflexion vs retry vs baseline 三组对比
- 用 compact table（3-4 行）呈现核心数字
- 强调：retry 无效（44.5% ≈ 42.9%），reflexion 有限改善但 death dominance 不变（31.4% >> 16.3%）
- 简要方法描述：Reflexion (Shinn et al., NeurIPS 2023) 的 trial → self-reflection → retry with reflections 机制；Retry = 相同配置去掉 reflection text
- **注意空间**：论文已 8 页，需要紧凑。可以压缩其他部分或将部分内容移到 Appendix

### 2. Discussion 扩展：Non-triviality Evidence
在 Discussion 中加段落（Reviewer 建议的核心 defense against triviality）：

核心逻辑："If death avoidance were trivially obvious or easily fixable, then:
(a) scaling should fix it — 72B shows it doesn't (chemistry-mix 50% = 7B)
(b) simple retry should help — retry shows it doesn't (44.5% ≈ 42.9%)
(c) the result should be uniform across tasks — but find-non-living-thing shows 0% across all conditions

Only targeted cognitive intervention (self-correction via reflexion) partially reduces death rate, confirming it is a structural environmental property requiring qualitative rather than quantitative intervention."

### 3. Discussion 扩展：Testable Prediction
加 testable prediction："We predict that in any environment where one modality triggers irreversible catastrophic failures with severe penalties, death avoidance will dominate routing signal. The reflexion result further predicts that self-correction mechanisms can selectively reduce death-driven signal, but cannot eliminate structural death dominance."

### 4. Abstract/Introduction 简要更新
- Abstract: 加 1 句 reflexion/retry finding（如 "Agent improvement baselines (reflexion, retry) confirm death dominance is structural rather than remediable"）
- Introduction Contribution 更新：如果空间允许，加一条 contribution point

### 5. W7 (Router negative result) 补充
§3.6/§4.5 中现有的 router negative result 解释可引用 reflexion 结果作为补充证据："Even with reflexion-level agent improvement, death asymmetry persists (31.4% vs 16.3%), confirming that the routing ceiling is structural."

## 约束
- 正文不超过 8 页（ARR 限制）
- 如果新内容超 8 页，将部分现有内容（如某些 robustness 细节）移到 Appendix
- 无 em-dash，无 -ing phrase 结尾
- 数字精度与现有表格一致
- 引用 Shinn et al. (2023) "Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning" NeurIPS 2023

完成后提交 R17 审稿验证。

\section{Introduction}

Large language models deployed as interactive agents must repeatedly decide \emph{how} to compute: reason internally, or delegate to an external tool.
A Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct agent navigating ScienceWorld \cite{scienceworld-2022}, a text-based science simulation with 30 task types, faces this choice at every step. Tracking temperature thresholds, container states, and multi-step procedures via internal reasoning is error-prone: the model may hallucinate that water has boiled when the stove was never activated, or that an object has been moved when the action was invalid. Deterministic external computation (environment simulators, code interpreters) eliminates such hallucinations via exact state transitions. The practical question for agent design is therefore: \emph{when should an agent route computation externally versus reasoning internally?}

Existing routing approaches frame this as a capability or efficiency decision.
Toolformer \cite{toolformer-2023} teaches models to insert API calls when doing so reduces perplexity; ART \cite{art-2023} decomposes tasks into tool-augmented programs; Chameleon \cite{chameleon-2023} selects among heterogeneous modules (search, code, vision) per subtask.
More recent adaptive-computation methods route to different reasoning depths \cite{cogrouter-2026,ares-2026} or model tiers \cite{mtrouter-2026}.
The shared assumption is that routing signal stems from diverse sources (accuracy, latency, capability matching) and that a learned router can exploit this signal to improve over any fixed strategy.
But this assumption has never been systematically verified: \emph{what actually drives the value of routing decisions in interactive environments?}
If routing value traces to a single failure mode, practitioners can replace complex learned routers with simpler safety-aware policies at lower computational cost and deployment risk.

We propose a \emph{formal diagnostic framework} for answering this question. The framework comprises (i)~episode-level counterfactual labeling under pure strategies (\S\ref{sec:collection}--\ref{sec:labeling}), and (ii)~the Death Avoidance Factor (DAF), a penalty-dependent metric that decomposes the routing score gap into death-avoidance and non-death components (\S\ref{sec:daf}). Applied to ScienceWorld, \textbf{78.9\% of non-tie routing labels arise from death asymmetry} (75 of 95), a penalty-independent finding that holds regardless of how death is penalized. Under ScienceWorld's specific penalty structure ($P{=}100$), the penalty-weighted DAF reaches $90.4\%$ (95\% CI: $[81.6\%, 98.8\%]$), consistent with the predicted value from observed $\delta{=}0.265$ and $P{=}100$.
The internal strategy's hallucination-induced failures trigger catastrophic agent death (a $-100$ penalty), while the deterministic strategy survives the same episodes.
Once death episodes are removed, the performance gap collapses to $\Delta_{\text{nd}} = +2.84$. A per-task consistency check ($r = 0.97$) confirms that the near-perfect correlation is a mathematical consequence of death dominance when $P$ is constant (\S\ref{sec:death-decomp}).

This framework addresses a methodological gap.
The standard approach to generating routing labels, per-step oracle comparison, degenerates under sparse rewards.
In ScienceWorld, non-zero reward arrives only at episode termination; 97.4\% of steps (across 11 prescreened task types) produce identical scores regardless of modality, so no step-level signal exists (\S\ref{sec:collection}).
Keyword-based heuristics also fail structurally, as ScienceWorld actions lack science-specific terminology (\S\ref{sec:baselines}).
Our counterfactual approach runs complete episodes under pure-internal (ReAct \cite{react-2023}) and pure-deterministic strategies, then compares episode outcomes to generate routing labels (\S\ref{sec:collection}). The framework is applicable to any environment with controllable modality comparison and binary catastrophic outcomes, requiring only paired episode outcomes under two modalities.

\section{Conclusion}

We presented a formal diagnostic framework for decomposing routing signal in modular LLM agents via episode-level counterfactual analysis with dual metrics (penalty-independent label fraction and penalty-dependent DAF). Applied to 245 ScienceWorld episodes (11 of 30 task types, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct), death asymmetry accounts for 78.9\% of non-tie routing labels; DAF $= 90.4\%$ at $P{=}100$ (95\% CI: $[81.6\%, 98.8\%]$). Cross-domain contrasts support framework predictions: MATH shows no routing signal without catastrophic failure; ALFWorld provides an illustrative contrast where information asymmetry drives routing under different modality definitions; a preliminary Llama pilot ($N{=}70$) shows directional consistency across model families. Open directions include replication in catastrophic-failure environments (e.g., NetHack~\citep{nethack-2020}, Crafter~\citep{crafter-2022}) and stronger backbones, which the framework predicts will lower DAF.

The $-100$ death penalty amplifies DAF; environments with softer penalties would exhibit lower DAF values (Appendix~\ref{app:penalty}). Cross-environment analyses on MATH and ALFWorld (\S\ref{sec:cross-env}, \S\ref{sec:discussion}) provide preliminary supporting evidence but do not conclusively establish generalization. The Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct pilot (7 task types, $N{=}70$; Appendix~\ref{app:cross-model}) confirms direction-consistent death patterns, though both models are in the 7--8B parameter range; validation at larger scales remains future work.
